landing.codecIntro: The system chooses a method that fits the source and avoids converting files again when possible.
landing.codecMp4Summary: Creates an MP4 that works on common devices and keeps the original picture when possible.
landing.codecMp4ConvertLabel: When conversion to MP4 is needed
landing.codecMp4ConvertDescription: H.264 (libx264) encodes the picture; AAC encodes the sound at 320 kb/s.

landing.codecMp4ExistingDescription: The original video codec is kept; when tracks are merged, only the sound may be converted to AAC.
landing.codecMp3Summary: Extracts high-quality MP3 audio. The file size depends on the source audio.
landing.codecMp3ConvertLabel: When conversion to MP3 is needed
landing.codecMp3ConvertDescription: Uses LAME (libmp3lame). The -qscale:a 0 setting selects the highest audio quality (0); VBR (variable bit rate) adjusts data per second to the audio, averaging about 245 kb/s.
landing.codecMp3ExistingLabel: If the source is already MP3
landing.codecMp3ExistingDescription: Keeps the original audio without re-encoding.
landing.codecGifSummary: Creates a GIF at up to 15 frames per second and 960 pixels wide.
landing.codecGifConvertLabel: When conversion to GIF is needed
landing.codecGifConvertDescription: Limited to 15 fps (frames per second), 960 px wide, and 256 colors. sierra2_4a is a dithering method that helps colors look smoother when the palette is reduced.
landing.codecGifExistingLabel: If the source is already GIF
landing.codecGifExistingDescription: Keeps the original file without converting it again.

how.title: How processing and file delivery work
how.intro: Media Loader processes source media on a server, then sends the selected output to your device. These two data transfers do not mean the browser downloads the file twice.
how.step1Title: 1. Fetch source media to the server
how.step1Description: After link and policy checks and your rights confirmation, the job enters a queue. A worker fetches media from its source through a proxy that validates network destinations, then keeps it temporarily in processing storage.
how.step2Description: The worker may merge audio and video tracks or convert the media to MP4, MP3, or GIF. The output size can differ from the source or the estimate shown before the job starts.
how.step3Title: 3. Deliver the output to your browser
how.step3Description: When processing finishes, the web app sends the output to your browser once. On mobile, the app may open a save or share sheet. If you close the app first, you can find the completed file in History.
how.whyTitle: Why do some websites appear to download only once?
how.whyDescription: Some services let the browser fetch a file directly from its source. Others send the source through a server to the browser as one stream. Either can appear as a single browser download; the page alone cannot show whether the service relayed or converted the media.
how.whyServerTitle: Why Media Loader uses a server worker
how.whyServerDescription: Media Loader lets its worker fetch the source and prepare the output on the server before delivery to your browser begins. This keeps queued work trackable, supports merging or conversion, and lets you return to History for the finished file. It uses additional server bandwidth and temporary storage, with one transfer from the source to the server and another from the server to your device.
how.transferQuestionTitle: Is the file downloaded to my device twice?
how.transferQuestionDescription: No. A worker fetches the source media to the server and prepares the output there first. Your browser receives only the final output once.
how.closePageQuestionTitle: Can I close the page while a job is processing?
how.closePageQuestionDescription: Yes. After a job enters the queue, the worker continues processing it on the server. You can return to History to track the job and retrieve the file when it is ready.
how.outputSizeQuestionTitle: Why is the final file size different from the estimate?
how.outputSizeQuestionDescription: The displayed size is an estimate based on the source and selected format. Merging audio and video tracks or converting the file can change the final output size.
how.formatsQuestionTitle: How do I choose MP4 video, MP3 audio, or GIF?
how.formatsQuestionDescription: Available options depend on the link and analysis result. MP4 is for video, MP3 extracts audio when a clip has sound, and GIF appears only when the system detects GIF media. Some sources may not offer every format.
how.supportedLinksQuestionTitle: Can I use private links or any website?
how.supportedLinksQuestionDescription: Only public links from supported sources are accepted. The service does not access private media or bypass sign-in pages or DRM.
how.accountAndRightsQuestionTitle: Why must I sign in and confirm rights before starting a job?
how.accountAndRightsQuestionDescription: Signing in links jobs to your account and keeps them in your history. Before queueing, you must confirm that you have the right to use the media under the service terms.
how.retentionQuestionTitle: How long can I download a completed file?
how.retentionQuestionDescription: Output files are stored temporarily for 60 minutes by default, then removed. Job history details may remain after the file is deleted. The actual retention period depends on the service configuration.
